Photograph: NSW Police View image in fullscreen The body of Lily Hooper has been found in Nattai national park in the NSW southern highlands. Photograph: NSW Police New South Wales Missing teen hiker Lily Hooper found dead as NSW police apologise for miscommunication ‘born of elation’ Initial report from ‘thick and dense terrain’ where Hooper was located was she had been found alive but within 10 minutes a ‘more accurate account’ was relayed to police Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Ima Caldwell and Luca Ittimani Thu 20 Aug 2026 05.34 EDT First published on Wed 19 Aug 2026 22.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The body of missing 18-year-old bushwalker Lily Hooper has been found in a remote New South Wales national park more than a week after she set out on her hike. Police have apologised “unreservedly” for wrongly suggesting Hooper had been alive when she was found by SES search volunteers off the walking trail in the state’s southern highlands on Thursday morning. The assistant commissioner Joe Cassar said SES search volunteers initially reported at 11.30am that the teenager had been found alive in “thick and dense terrain” in Nattai national park about 90km south-west of Sydney . However, within 10 minutes, the search crew relayed a “more accurate account” to police confirming Hooper was dead. “There’s no playbook to communication,” Cassar told reporters in Moss Vale on Thursday afternoon. Her body was not expected to be retrieved for many hours, NSW police said. The commissioner, Mal Lanyon, told reporters in Goulburn on Thursday the miscommunication about Hooper being found was “born out of elation”. “Tragically that miscommunication then led to a deflation and obviously, we know now, an impact on her family,” Lanyon said. “I unashamedly apologise for any additional trauma that may have caused Lily’s family, but certainly for the embarrassment and confusion that caused.” The assistant commissioner said Hooper’s parents had been at the search command post and were being kept “well informed” by police. The family was told of the initial report that Hooper was alive before the devastating update came through from the scene using hand-held radios. “I cannot turn the clock back,” Cassar said. “If we were able to provide them more detailed information on that first report, I can tell you that would have been the case.” Trail map Earlier on Thursday, police had told media a “hiker” had been found after the multi-agency search and the NSW premier, Chris Minns, told parliament Hooper had been “found alive” with half a bottle of water. But a short time later, Minns announced: “I’ve got some terrible news. I apologise … Lily’s body has been found.” Minns later said in a statement he had received incorrect advice and “genuinely believed” he was sharing good news. “My deepest condolences are with Lily’s family,” the premier said. “I am profoundly sorry to think that anything I said may have added to their heartbreak at an already devastating time.” Hooper was found off the trail a “significant distance” from her car, which was parked near the trail head on Wanganderry Road at High Range, Cassar said. The assistant commissioner said it was not yet clear how she died or if she had sustained injuries. He said her body would likely be brought out by foot as air retrieval was “exceptionally difficult”. A report will be prepared for the coroner, investigating the time, place and circumstances of Hooper’s death, as well as the search and communications issues. Cassar said criminal investigators from the Hume police district were gathering evidence in line with police protocol. Location map Hooper left her Sydney home on Wednesday 12 August for the hike. Initial police inquiries suggested she reached the summit of Bonnum Pic mountain mid-morning on Wednesday, having sent messages from the trail earlier that day. She was reported missing when she did not return home that evening. Emergency services located her car late that night. Lanyon said nearly 1,000 people had joined the search on the ground over the last week. More than 100 ADF personnel had joined the search operation in the past 24 hours. The army personnel joined people from PolAir, NSW police, the SES, RFS, Fire and Rescue NSW, and the National Parks and Wildlife Service. A rescue helicopter and police helicopters were engaged. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Volunteers on the ground included Hooper’s family, family and Volunteer Rescue Association crews mobilised from as far north as Cessnock. The SES said 260 volunteer members trained in bush search and rescue were on the ground from Saturday to Thursday. On Monday, police said the search was focused on the lower sections of the Bonnum Pic walking trail. Police were uncertain what supplies Hooper had with her. Police have said Hooper was believed to have been an experienced hiker. The NSW police chief inspector Brendan Bernie said on Monday: “We’re hopefully relying on Lily’s experience to get her through this ordeal and [we] can locate her safely.” Poor weather over the weekend had hampered search operations in the already complex terrain. Outdoor recreation website AllTrails describes the Bonnum Pic hike as a “formidable challenge,” noting some hikers recommend using rope to negotiate “steep, exposed sections”. “Post-fire regrowth has made the trail overgrown and difficult to identify … [and] the path frequently disappears,” the site’s description reads. The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said on Thursday that Hooper’s death was an “unspeakable tragedy”. “Lily Hooper had so much more to offer the world,” Albanese said. “Her passing … will be felt very deeply across the southern highlands, among her family, her friends, and indeed right across the nation.” Angus Taylor, the federal opposition leader and the local MP for the electorate where the Hooper family live, paid tribute, too. “Any parent who reads this news will hug their children tighter tonight,” he said. “When they do, they will spare a thought and a prayer for Lily’s mother, father, and family who can’t do the same. We grieve for their most terrible loss.” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Explore more on these topics New South Wales news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story From ‘elation’ to ‘terrible news’ in 10 minutes: how the confusion over missing bushwalker Lily Hooper unfolded Two 17-year-olds from Sydney private school among three charged over alleged rape of teenage girl Catholic schools chief denies wiping critical evidence after performing factory reset on phone, Icac hears NSW judge says anti-Israel graffiti case went ‘haywire’ when vandalism was labelled antisemitic Five Sydney Swans players suspended for rest of AFL season say they are ‘deeply sorry’ Full Story Does Australia have a gun problem? – Full Story podcast Sydney Swans will sanction players for ‘serious breach’ over incident that led to sexual assault allegations Family of missing 18-year-old hiker ‘absolutely devastated’ as search continues in rugged NSW terrain Bondi library removes book How to Sell a Genocide from shelves after complaint Sydney Swans coach ‘extremely disappointed’ as club faces call on standing down players linked to alleged sexual assault Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

Photograph: House Of Commons/Reuters View image in fullscreen Ed Miliband said he would refuse to be a bystander to further suffering and the destruction of the two-state solution. Photograph: House Of Commons/Reuters Israel Analysis Ed Miliband has overturned decades of Foreign Office inertia on illegal Israeli settlements Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor Foreign secretary ends UK’s feigned helplessness with sanctions and condemnation of ‘ethnic cleansing’ Will UK sanctions have any impact on ‘settler terrorists’? Tue 8 Sep 2026 14.34 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 16.10 EDT Share The indefatigable ability of UK Foreign Office ministers over decades to issue boilerplate statements of concern about the extension of illegal settlements in Israel has long been a matter of ridicule. Even some of the Conservative ministers who issued them, notably Alan Duncan and Alistair Burt, have agreed. Duncan described the UK stance towards settlements as weak and naive, while Burt wondered at the ability of the Foreign Office to find new forms of diplomatic condemnation that never amounted to any specific action. Margaret Thatcher, often torn as prime minister between her natural sympathy for Israel and her fear of the Gulf states falling under the sway of the Soviet Union, similarly expressed her anger at the settlements. But in the face of the Israeli disillusionment with a two-state solution – to which the UK had been committed at the UN since 1946, if not before – the UK produced little practical policy to prevent the spread of Israel’s illegal settlements. The UK-Israel trade agreement prevented preferential tariffs applying to goods coming from territories brought under Israeli administration after June 1967. The business department also advised companies not to trade with the settlements – but many simply ignored the advice or, to secure the preferential tariff, relabelled their goods as from Israel. The then trade minister Chris Bryant told the business select committee in June it was very difficult to be certain of the origin of goods. At the same time, the legal advice was that the UK regime could place sanctions on entities only if they were linked to settler violence, but could not put a contractor under sanctions simply for working on settlements. View image in fullscreen Young Palestinians look at a new Israeli settlement from the Palestinian village of Duma, near Nablus, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank in February 2026. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters It was this unhappy moral and legal mess that Ed Miliband inherited. As soon as he took office as foreign secretary, he said he refused to be a bystander to further suffering and the destruction of the two-state solution that settlement expansion represented. In this he had the support of the prime minister, Andy Burnham. Above all, Miliband felt that the UK could not feign powerlessness, and to do so, or pay lip service to action, would prove disastrous to Israel’s own future. He was perhaps the only front-rank Labour politician who could push this argument through at such pace, overturning the inertia and caution built into Foreign Office legal advice. His Jewish heritage – his mother, Marion Kozak, was a Holocaust survivor who fled to Israel – his life growing up with the Palestinian question and empathy for those subjected to antisemitism put him in a near unimpeachable position to adopt the role of Israel’s critical friend. The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, might this week say the Labour government is gripped by Jew-hatred, a charge he laid at Miliband’s door knowing he is Jewish, but Miliband’s riposte is simple. The best route to Israel’s security lay in Palestinian self-determination and the introduction of the two-state solution in its fullest form. To equate Israel only with the current Likud-led government as too many Conservatives have been prone to do, was a category error, he said: “Holding Jewish people responsible for the actions of the Israeli government is antisemitism, plain and simple.” He is thus the first UK foreign secretary to describe what is happening in the West Bank as ethnic cleansing , and in so doing to in effect to accuse Israel of turning a blind eye to acts that amount to war crimes. Miliband also ended the two years of delay in responding to the international court of justice advisory opinion in June 2024 that the occupation is unlawful. In what he admitted was an overdue statement of reality, he accepted the ICJ opinion that the occupation, and not just the settlements, were so designated. Accepting the ICJ opinion arguably places stronger obligations on the UK government to not assist the occupation. It may help to explain why the trade ban extends into services such as providing insurance for illegal settlements. View image in fullscreen Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel and a steadfast supporter of the Netanyahu government, has previously claimed that Ed Miliband hates Jews. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images The biggest diplomatic rabbit Miliband pulled from the hat was the agreement of France and Canada to impose similar trade bans . France took the lead last year on recognition of Palestine; this year, it is the turn of the UK to lead on following through on the consequences of that recognition. Paris appears to have been persuaded by the UK to stop waiting for the EU to reach an agreement on collective action, since it seemed unlikely the opposition in Germany and indifference in parts of the European Commission would end. A group of countries imposing the trade ban together of course makes Israeli reprisals harder, and serves to underline Israel’s isolation. The perceived weaknesses are obvious. Miliband still left it to the international courts to determine whether a genocide occurred in Gaza, something that might not be adjudicated for at least five years. There was mounting evidence of ethnic cleansing in Gaza, he said, but again it was for the courts to determine if that was so. There is no pledge to protect the international court of justice or the international criminal court from the US drive to render them inoperable. As to a UK arms sales ban, an exemption continues for the sale of parts for F35 jet planes to the main US spares pool – all on the basis the F-35 jets “do not materially support the occupation” – the criteria the foreign secretary has set. Miliband specifically condemned the Boycott, Disinvestment and Sanctions movement because it targets the whole Israeli economy and not just the occupied territories. The secondary legislation required to make sanctions as wide as envisaged may take as long as nine months, contrasting with the speed with which sanctions were enforced against Russia over the annexation of Crimea. But to focus solely on what is absent is to miss the moment. Duncan, for instance, said: “At last, in the face of state-backed terrorism by illegal settlers, the British government has shown unprecedented moral courage.” There is a risk of a cascading backlash from the White House – but Trump, trapped in a political labyrinth after he was persuaded to attack Iran, has little reason to come to Benjamin Netanyahu’s aid. Miliband has taken a risk, but after more than 70,000 deaths in Gaza, and the two-state solution on life support, it may be time to dare. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/19/trum.text: Menü Kereső Trump aláírta, jöhetnek az amerikai szankciók Oroszország ellen Külföld Molnár Zoltán Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Aláírta Donald Trump amerikai elnök pénteken azt a törvényt, ami lehetőséget ad az Egyesült Államoknak arra, hogy széles körű szankciókkal gyakoroljon nyomást Oroszországra az Ukrajna elleni háború befejezéséért. A kongresszus két nappal korábban véglegesítette a jogszabályt , ami az orosz energia- és hadiipart, valamint az olajszállító árnyékflottát is célba veszi – írja az MTI. A jogszabály felhatalmazza Trumpot, hogy akár 100 százalékos büntetővámot vessen ki az orosz energiahordozók öt legnagyobb vásárlójának, illetve az Oroszországgal szembeni energiaszankciók megkerülését leginkább segítő öt országnak az Egyesült Államokba irányuló importjára. A listát 180 naponta újra meghatározzák. A finn központú CREA intézet augusztusi adatai szerint nyersolaj terén Kína, India, Törökország és az EU, tengeren szállított LNG-földgáz terén ezeken felül Japán és Dél-Korea, csővezetéken szállított gáz terén pedig a fentiek mellett Szerbia és Moldova eshet a top 5-be. A szankciók között szerepel az orosz elnök, Vlagyimir Putyin, valamint több katonai vezető amerikai beutazásának megtiltása és esetleges amerikai vagyoni érdekeltségeik befagyasztása is. Hasonló intézkedések vonatkozhatnak egyes orosz pénzügyi intézményekre. A törvényt a nemrég meghalt Lindsey Graham republikánus szenátor kezdeményezte, és hivatalosan az ő nevét is viseli. Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök péntek éjjel üdvözölte a jogszabály aláírását, és megköszönte a kongresszus támogatását is. Az X-en közzétett bejegyzésében azt írta: amikor Graham Ukrajnában járt, mindig beszélt arról, mennyire fontos, hogy ne enyhüljön a nyomás Oroszországon, mert ez az út vezethet el a békéhez. Fegyvercsomag Ukrajnának Eközben az amerikai külügyminisztérium pénteken jóváhagyta korszerű légvédelmi rendszerek, az ehhez kapcsolódó felszerelések és szolgáltatások lehetséges eladását Ukrajnának 2,68 milliárd dollár értékben. A külügyminisztérium szerint még szükség van a kongresszus engedélyére is. A beszerzést az európai országok, valamint a Joe Biden volt amerikai elnök kormányzata alatt elkülönített amerikai külföldi katonai pénzügyi támogatás (FMF) kombinációjával finanszíroznák. A csaknem 2,7 milliárd dolláros csomag többek között S-300 légvédelmi rakétákból, GAM-67 rakétákból, megnövelt hatótávolságú légvédelmi lézerirányítású rakétarendszerekből, valamint drónellenes radarrendszerekből áll. https://www.politico.eu/article/emmanuel.text: French President Emmanuel Macron will “solemnly” address the French people Sunday evening following violent scenes across the country that resulted in hundreds of arrests and millions of euros in damage. Clashes broke out Saturday in France on the latest day of demonstrations that emerged from last month’s student protests, which had featured school blockades and calls for better study conditions. The movement has since grown into nationwide protests against rising living costs — and has become a political issue as the campaign for next year’s presidential election heats up. Footage showed widespread looting, burned-out cars and smashed store windows. Rioters set fire to the town hall in Limoges, a city in central France, causing the roof to partially collapse. One demonstrator died after suffering a heart attack. Advertisement Advertisement “More than 2,000 people have been taken into custody,” Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez wrote on X Sunday afternoon. “More than 600 police officers, gendarmes, and firefighters have been injured amid these scenes of violence.” Before addressing the nation at 8 p.m., Macron will meet Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and the ministers responsible for handling the crisis. U.S. President Donald Trump seized on the violence to blame migration. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform Sunday afternoon. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” he added. Earlier in the day, U.S. Vice President JD Vance had called out European leaders : “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion” but “ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.” He called on Americans to pay attention, as “this is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country.” The U.S. faces crucial midterm elections to both houses of Congress on Nov. 3. The French government has struggled to deal with the crisis in recent weeks — Lecornu described it as “urban violence” — and is now hoping the student movement will fade due to a two-week school holiday that started Friday. Guillaume Guérin, the mayor of Limoges, criticized the government’s handling of the demonstrations, saying the national police “simply had no more ammunition left.” Advertisement Advertisement
